citation.note: Wage Theft Prevention Act (Labor Law § 195): Mandatory written notice at hire and 7 days before any pay-rate decrease; notice of pay statements at each payday.
Salary history ban (§ 194-a): Cannot inquire about prior wages; retaliation for refusal prohibited.

body.context: setting compensation for a promotion or base-pay change

citation.note: Payroll and personnel record retention (§ 195(4), § 740): employers must retain wage and hour records for 6 years documenting hours worked, rates, deductions, and gross/net pay per employee; timekeeping records 6 years minimum.
Accrued Paid Sick Leave Handling (§ 196-b): track accrued sick leave (1 hour per 30 hours worked, 40-hour annual max); on promotion, carry the accrued balance forward without forfeiture.

body.interaction_rule: Accrued Paid Sick Leave Handling (§ 196-b): track accrued sick leave (1 hour per 30 hours worked, 40-hour annual max); on promotion, carry the accrued balance forward without forfeiture.

citation.note: Paid Family Leave Integration (Workers' Comp Law Art. 9): up to 12 weeks per calendar year at 67% of average weekly wage for bonding with a new child or caring for an ill family member; on promotion during active leave, ensure return to the promoted role and updated pay rate.

body.interaction_rule: Paid Family Leave (Workers' Comp Law Art. 9): up to 12 weeks per calendar year at 67% of average weekly wage for bonding or family care; on promotion during active leave, ensure return to the promoted role and updated pay rate.

citation.note: Paid Prenatal Leave (§ 196-c, effective 2025-01-01): up to 20 hours of paid leave in any 52-week period for prenatal appointments; on promotion during leave, carry the balance and apply the promoted rate on return.

body.interaction_rule: Paid Prenatal Leave (§ 196-c, effective 2025-01-01): up to 20 hours of paid leave in any 52-week period for prenatal appointments; on promotion during leave, carry the balance and apply the promoted rate on return.

citation.note: Manual workers must be paid weekly; other employees no less often than semi-monthly (Labor Law § 191).
Final wages are due on the next regular payday after any termination (Labor Law § 195).

body.deadline_description: Final wages are due on the next regular payday after any termination (Labor Law § 195).

citation.note: Pay Transparency (§ 194-b): employers with 4 or more employees must include good-faith wage ranges and job descriptions in all postings, promotion notices, and transfer opportunities; internal promotions require wage-range disclosure.

body.required_disclosure: Employers with 4 or more employees must include good-faith wage ranges (minimum and maximum at time of posting) and job descriptions in all postings, promotion notices, and transfer opportunities (Labor Law § 194-b).

citation.note: NY WARN Act (Labor Law Art. 25-A): employers with 50 or more employees must give 90 days advance written notice before a mass layoff, plant closing, or mass termination affecting 25+ employees in 30 days; violations carry $10,000/day penalties plus mandatory severance of 1 week per year of service.

body.note: NY WARN Act (Labor Law Art. 25-A): employers with 50 or more employees must give 90 days advance written notice before a mass layoff, plant closing, or mass termination affecting 25+ employees in 30 days; violations carry $10,000/day penalties plus mandatory severance of 1 week per year of service.

citation.note: Regional minimum wage tiers (Labor Law § 652, effective 2026): NYC/Long Island/Westchester $17.00/hour; rest of state $16.00/hour; frequent annual increases by CPI-W.
Regional minimum wage tiers (Labor Law § 652, effective 2026): rest of state $16.00/hour; frequent annual increases by CPI-W.

Equal Pay (§ 194): unlawful to pay protected-class employees at lower rates for substantially similar work under comparable conditions. On promotion + base-pay change, identify peers performing substantially similar work and flag differentials without documented justification (skill differential, seniority, merit system).
Pay statement (§ 195(3)): an itemized statement must accompany each payment of wages showing gross pay, net pay, deductions, and the pay period covered.

Personnel-file access (proposed Labor Law § 210-b, S.3460/A.2107): passed the Senate and Assembly but the Governor's signature was unconfirmed as of last verification, so this is not current law. If signed, employers must provide a personnel-record copy within 5 business days of a written request at no cost.

Retaliation is prohibited for reporting violations or filing complaints with the Department of Labor (Labor Law § 215, 6-year statute of limitations); whistleblower protection covers reporting violations of law (Labor Law § 740 as amended 2022).

Cannabis: Employers cannot take adverse action based solely on detection of cannabis metabolites from lawful off-duty use (Executive Law § 201-d, as amended); may test for on-the-job impairment or reasonable suspicion.

citation.section: Information Security Breach and Notification Act
citation.note: Data breach notification (NYS Information Security Breach and Notification Act, effective 2025-03-21): applies to any breach of personal information (name plus financial account, SSN, health/medical info, or biometric records) by an unauthorized person; carry a 30-day operational notification target pending counsel confirmation of the statutory window.

Electronic monitoring (Civil Rights Law § 201-i, effective 2022-05-07): employers who monitor telephone conversations, email, or internet access must provide written notice to new hires and current employees, obtain acknowledgment, and post the notice in a conspicuous workplace location.

Automated Employment Decision Tool Notice (NYC Local Law 144, effective 2023-01-01): employers using AEDTs for hiring or promotion must commission an independent annual bias audit, post the audit summary, and provide 10 business days notice to candidates before tool use.
